This module introduces no new CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) citation and no new external
source — it's pure synthesis, applying 164.306(d)(3), 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D), 164.402(2), and
164.414(b), all already fetched, verified, and quoted in full in earlier modules of this course.
No new source was independently fetched this session, consistent with how this curriculum has
handled prior synthesis-only closing modules (see `grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`'s
`poams-and-capas` resources page for the same pattern). The links below point back to this
course's own earlier modules — the actual sources behind everything this module reused.

- **[Information Governance in a Covered Entity](../information-governance-in-a-covered-entity/index.qmd)**
  — module 1. This is where the Brookfield laptop incident and all of its locked facts were
  first logged: the six-field, ~212-donor extract, the encryption-status ambiguity, and the
  clean-population finding this module's investigation never touched or reopened.

- **[Security Rule Safeguards and Part 11](../security-rule-safeguards-and-part-11/index.qmd)**
  — module 3. The source of 164.306(d)(3) and 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D), both reused (not re-quoted
  at length) in this module, and of the original finding — Lakeshore's encryption *policy* was
  sound, its *verification* for this one device was not — that this module's investigation set
  out to test further.

- **[Breach Notification and Dual Reporting](../breach-notification-and-dual-reporting/index.qmd)**
  — module 4. The source of 164.402's four-factor test and 164.414(b)'s burden of proof, both
  reused in this module, and of the provisional breach determination this module's investigation
  was built to confirm, rebut, or honestly leave standing. It now stands as this course's final
  determination.

If a future session needs to go beyond what this course's own four modules already sourced —
for example, 164.412's law-enforcement-delay mechanics, or HHS's own specified encryption
methodology referenced in 164.402's "unsecured protected health information" definition — run
`fetch-source` first rather than asserting anything about either one from memory.
